actions.justification: MANDATORY action — activate stroke team immediately. Patient presents with right hemiparesis and confusion after seizure, suspected stroke. Time-critical window for tPA requires immediate team mobilization.
Critical for tPA eligibility — must establish exact time of symptom onset or last known well to determine if patient is within the 4.5-hour window. Seizure onset was 20 minutes ago per witness.

Hypoglycemia is a reversible stroke mimic that must be ruled out immediately. Patient also has epilepsy, which can cause post-ictal (Todd's) paralysis — glucose check is essential before pursuing tPA pathway.

Non-contrast CT head is the most critical immediate action to rule out intracranial hemorrhage before tPA consideration. Per AHA stroke guidelines, CT must be obtained before any thrombolytic therapy. This also helps differentiate stroke from Todd's paralysis post-seizure.
NIHSS quantifies stroke severity, guides tPA eligibility and treatment decisions, and provides baseline for monitoring neurological progression. Essential for documentation and treatment planning.

Urgent neurology consultation is critical given the complex presentation: seizure with post-ictal Todd's paralysis must be differentiated from acute ischemic stroke. Neurology expertise is essential for tPA eligibility determination given the epilepsy comorbidity and seizure at onset.
PT/INR and PTT are required before tPA administration to rule out coagulopathy contraindications. Patient has epilepsy and may be on antiepileptic drugs; need to verify no anticoagulation use.
Platelet count is mandatory before tPA eligibility determination. Thrombocytopenia (<100,000) is a contraindication to IV alteplase per AHA guidelines.

CTA of head and neck is indicated to identify large vessel occlusion (LVO). If LVO is present, patient may be eligible for mechanical thrombectomy in addition to or instead of tPA. Also helps distinguish stroke from Todd's paralysis post-seizure.

MRI DWI provides superior sensitivity for acute ischemic stroke, especially in the setting of post-ictal Todd's paralysis (patient has epilepsy) which must be differentiated from true ischemic stroke. This will help confirm the working diagnosis before considering tPA.

Patient is at 45 minutes from arrival with suspected acute ischemic stroke within the 4.5-hour tPA window. CT head already obtained (no hemorrhage assumed if proceeding), labs completed, BP 155/88 is within acceptable range (<185/110). Administer IV alteplase 0.9mg/kg if eligibility criteria are confirmed (no contraindications from history, normal coagulation, normal glucose, no hemorrhage on CT). Note: epilepsy alone is not a contraindication; post-ictal hemiparesis must be weighed against ischemic stroke risk.

Given NIHSS already calculated and CTA already completed, if large vessel occlusion is identified on CTA, mechanical thrombectomy should be arranged concurrently with tPA consideration to minimize door-to-puncture time per AHA stroke guidelines.
Point-of-care glucose check is mandatory to rule out hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic, especially critical given epilepsy history. Must be done immediately.
IV access is mandatory for medication administration including tPA if eligible, and for IV fluids/emergency drugs. Must be established now.
Formal bedside NIHSS score is mandatory to quantify stroke severity, guide tPA eligibility, and determine thrombectomy candidacy. Required per AHA stroke guidelines.

Critical for tPA eligibility - must confirm exact time of symptom onset. Patient had witnessed seizure 20 minutes ago but last known well time may differ. tPA window is 4.5 hours from last known well. This is a mandatory action not yet completed with this specific action_id.

Mandatory STAT non-contrast CT head to rule out hemorrhagic stroke before any thrombolytic therapy. While order_imaging_ct_head was done, order_stat_ct_head is the required action_id in this phase to confirm results are available for tPA decision-making at 75 minutes.

Mandatory action - 12-lead ECG needed to detect atrial fibrillation (cardioembolic source) and other cardiac arrhythmias. AF would guide anticoagulation strategy post-stroke. This is a required step per AHA stroke guidelines.

Mandatory action: Complete CBC/BMP/coagulation panel to confirm platelet count, electrolytes, and coagulation status for tPA eligibility assessment. Although individual components were ordered, this consolidated panel is the required mandatory action for this phase.
Assess pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale to establish baseline functional status, which is required for tPA eligibility and treatment decision-making per AHA stroke guidelines.
Assess ASPECTS score on the CT head already obtained to evaluate extent of early ischemic changes, guiding tPA and thrombectomy eligibility per AHA stroke guidelines.

BP is 155/88 mmHg which is within tPA eligibility range (<185/110). Serial vital sign monitoring is essential post-tPA administration and to ensure BP remains controlled. This is a key ongoing assessment in the acute stroke protocol.

Per AHA stroke guidelines, after IV alteplase administration (already completed), patient must be admitted to ICU or stroke unit for protocolized monitoring including neuro checks q15min and BP monitoring q15min x2h then q30min x6h.
